reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Counting old infarcts as acute change.
Reporting the total without the affected regions.
name: Posterior Circulation ASPECTS

version.label: pc-ASPECTS (Puetz et al. 2008)
version.detail: 10 points: thalami, cerebellar hemispheres and PCA territories 1 point each; midbrain and pons 2 points each.

purpose: Quantifies the extent of early ischaemic change on non-contrast CT.
intendedPopulation: Adults with suspected acute posterior circulation ischaemic stroke.

calculatorNotice.title: Imaging score, not a treatment decision
calculatorNotice.message: Lower scores mean more extensive early ischaemic change. Treatment eligibility thresholds vary between trials and protocols and are not applied here.

inputDefinitions.label: Regions with early ischaemic change
inputDefinitions.help: Select every region with early ischaemic change (hypoattenuation or focal swelling). Select 'None' if no region is affected.

resultStates.label: No early ischaemic change
resultStates.summary: No early ischaemic change in the scored regions at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: A normal score does not exclude ischaemia: early CT changes can be absent or subtle.

resultStates.label: pc-ASPECTS {total}
resultStates.summary: Early ischaemic change reduces the score by {regions} point(s) from 10.
resultStates.detail: Interpret with timing, imaging modality and the clinical picture.

clinicalContext.text: A topographic CT score used to describe the extent of early ischaemia.
Commonly reported in acute stroke imaging and trials.

clinicalInsights.text: Thresholds used for treatment selection differ between trials and protocols; this app does not apply them.
Report which regions are affected, not only the total.

limitations.text: Early ischaemic changes are subtle; inter-rater agreement is moderate and improves with training and windowing.

limitations: Sensitive to time from onset and CT technique.
Equal weighting does not reflect the functional importance of each region.

confounders.effect: Very early scans may show little change.
Can be mistaken for acute change.
Reduces reliability, especially in the posterior fossa.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Vessel occlusion status or collateral flow.

guideSections.what: A 10-point topographic score for the posterior circulation.
guideSections.whenToUse: Initial non-contrast CT in suspected acute ischaemic stroke.
guideSections.howToPerform: Subtract the weight of each affected region from 10: 1 point for each thalamus, cerebellar hemisphere and PCA territory; 2 points for any midbrain or pons involvement.
guideSections.clinicalContext: One imaging descriptor among several; decisions integrate clinical, imaging and timing information.

sources.citation: Puetz V, Sylaja PN, Coutts SB, et al. Extent of hypoattenuation on CT angiography source images predicts functional outcome in patients with basilar artery occlusion. Stroke. 2008;39(9):2485-2490.
